# parity-fuzz --mode rcexpand baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode rcexpand --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (the mode opened at 228). Covers
# RC_EXPAND_PARAM (the `^` flag / plan9, c:Src/subst.c:2550-2557) and its
# sibling unbraced flag `=` (SH_WORD_SPLIT / spbreak, c:2558-2569), each paired
# with its braced form. That pairing is the load-bearing part: C runs ONE flag
# loop for braced and unbraced alike (the paramsubst-start guard admits the flag
# char at c:1890-1891), so `$^a` and `${^a}` must agree exactly — whereas this
# port reaches them through different code, which is exactly how the unbraced
# forms came to compile to literal text.
#
# Every divergence this mode found was a real port bug and was FIXED:
#
#   1. The UNBRACED `$^a` form did not exist; it compiled to LITERAL text, so
#      promptinit:23's `$^fpath/prompt_*_setup(N)` found ZERO themes where zsh
#      finds 18. 29 of zsh's own shipped functions use it, `_git` among them.
#   2. `$=s` worked ONLY as a whole word: `pre$=s` / `$=s.x` / `$==s.x` were
#      literal text, because a fast path keyed on `untoked.starts_with("$=")`
#      with an all-alphanumeric name cannot express an affix.
#   3. Double quotes JOIN before plan9 runs (c:3029-3036), so `"pre${^b}"` is
#      ONE word.
#   4. `${^^a}` sets plan9 = 0 and NOTHING else (c:2553-2555), and must override
#      the rcexpandparam OPTION (c:2554).
#   5. An EMPTY array under plan9 DELETES the whole word (c:4362-4365).
#   6. An EMPTY ELEMENT drops from an unquoted splat (c:184-188) — but only as a
#      standalone word: with an affix the cross-product runs first and makes it
#      non-empty (`x${^a}y` → `xay xy xby`).
#   7. prefork's empty-word delete (c:184-188) must run AFTER the word is
#      ASSEMBLED, not at the split. For `s=' a b '` the split leaves an empty
#      field at each end and an affix attaches to the one on ITS side, so only
#      the FAR-side empty goes:
#        ${=s}.x  → `a` `b` `.x`   (trailing empty became .x, leading deleted)
#        pre${=s} → `pre` `a` `b`  (leading empty became pre, trailing deleted)
#      Dropping before the concat would delete the field the affix lands on.
#   8. `${==s}` forces NO split (c:2560-2564 `spbreak = 0`), but an unquoted
#      expansion that comes out EMPTY is still an empty WORD that prefork
#      deletes: `s=''; r=(${==s})` has ZERO elements. Every other form got this
#      for free (`$v`, `${v}`, `${=s}` are all 0); only the no-split arm
#      returned Value::Str("") and kept the word. Quoted `"${==s}"` correctly
#      keeps its one empty word.
#
# Structural note, since it caused most of the above: the `^` / `=` flags are
# known only at COMPILE time while every concat builtin dispatched on the
# RUNTIME option (`plan9_active()`), so a flag could neither override its option
# nor reuse the option path's already-correct logic. Fixed with two sibling
# builtins — BUILTIN_CONCAT_PLAN9 (→ concat_plan9: C's c:4316-4350 cartesian
# emit plus the c:4362 word deletion) and BUILTIN_CONCAT_SPLICE_NOPLAN9 (→
# concat_splice: C's non-plan9 c:4366-4437) — chosen by is_plan9_expansion /
# is_plan9_off_expansion. They cannot reuse CONCAT_DISTRIBUTE_FORCED: that also
# serves `${(@)a}` / `${(f)v}` / `${a[@]}`, which KEEP the word when the array
# is empty (`x${(@)a}y` → `xy`) where plan9 deletes it.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
